players.product: electrical and mechanical construction and installation of data-center power and cooling systems

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 revenues were a quarterly record of $4.63 billion, up 19.7% (organic 16.8%), with operating income of $403.8 million (8.7% margin) and diluted EPS of $6.84 (+30%). Electrical Construction revenues were $1.45 billion (+33.1%) at a 12.1% operating margin; Mechanical Construction revenues were $2.03 billion (+28.9%) at a 10.9% margin, down from 11.9% on mix (more construction-manager/prime work and more GMP or cost-plus projects).
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 revenues $4.63 billion (+19.7%, organic 16.8%); operating income $403.8 million (8.7%); Electrical $1.45 billion (+33.1%); Mechanical $2.03 billion (+28.9%), margin 10.9% vs 11.9%

quarterly_data.signal: Data centers drove both construction segments: electrical network and communications revenues rose nearly 50% (2/3 of the segment's growth), and mechanical network and communications revenues rose 86%. CFO Jason Nalbandian: 'Increased cooling requirements and advancements in liquid cooling, particularly for AI data centers, continued to drive opportunities for this segment.' In round numbers network and communications revenue was up $240 million in electrical and $280 million in mechanical.
quarterly_data.figure: mechanical network and communications revenue +86%; electrical nearly 50%; up $240 million electrical, $280 million mechanical

quarterly_data.signal: RPOs reached $15.62 billion vs $11.75 billion a year earlier and $13.25 billion at December 31, 2025 (+32.9% YoY, +17.9% sequential), with 'particularly robust activity in network communications or data centers'. CEO Tony Guzzi: 'We see no sign of slowing demand in this vertical, where customer investments in AI infrastructure, cloud infrastructure, and overall digital transformation are driving unprecedented levels of activity.' CFO: 78% of RPO burns within 12 months (vs 82% at year-end), and on the portion extending past 2026: 'If you look at our total RPO, I'd be surprised if $6 billion-$6.5 billion goes even into 2027.'
quarterly_data.figure: RPO $15.62 billion (+32.9% YoY, +17.9% sequential); 78% burns within 12 months; 'surprised if $6 billion-$6.5 billion goes even into 2027'

quarterly_data.signal: EMCOR raised full-year 2026 guidance to revenues of $18.5 billion-$19.25 billion and diluted EPS of $28.25-$29.75, citing its strong start and RPO. CFO: at the revenue midpoint EMCOR still needs to book about 30% of its work (down from 40%-45% at the start of the year); where it lands depends on how quickly newly booked jobs mobilize. Strong execution gives 'the opportunity to replicate last year's record margins at 9.4%'.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 revenues $18.5 billion-$19.25 billion; EPS $28.25-$29.75; still need to book about 30%

quarterly_data.signal: Guzzi: versus a year ago the RPO mix has moved 'a little more to GMP', mainly in mechanical, driven by larger scopes 'because of the power requirements and the interact cooling we're doing, which is driven primarily, which we think, by AI data centers', including 'large language model data centers' sited for access to power. Customers start AI data center jobs as GMP while designs evolve, and the CFO said two customers simply prefer GMP work. Management said it takes this work because it drives more margin dollars.

Capacity limits: Guzzi said growth is 'emphatically not' limited by equipment procurement because 'on data centers, most of the major equipment is being bought by the owners or the owners through the GCs'; the bottleneck is field leadership (foremen, general foremen, project managers). He reported no notable change in craft labor tightness. CFO: 2026 capex of somewhere between $115 million and $125 million, a significant part fitting out or upgrading prefabrication facilities; over three years capex is growing at twice the revenue rate.
